🥘 Ingredients

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour, sifted
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup buttermilk, room temperature
  • 1/3 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled
  • 1 large egg, room temperature
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 tablespoon lemon zest, finely grated
  • 1 1/2 cups fresh blueberries

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners or grease it lightly. This step is crucial because a properly preheated oven ensures even baking and a nice rise. Using liners makes cleanup easier and keeps muffins from sticking. Avoid skipping the preheat because a cold oven will cause uneven texture and dense muffins.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the sifted flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Sifting helps aerate the flour and evenly distribute the leavening agents, which leads to a lighter muffin. Mixing the dry ingredients first also prevents overmixing later when combined with wet ingredients.
  3. In a separate bowl, whisk the buttermilk, melted butter, egg, vanilla extract, and lemon zest until smooth. Combining wet ingredients separately allows for better emulsification and ensures the lemon zest flavor is evenly dispersed throughout the batter.
  4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and gently fold together using a spatula. Mix just until combined; it’s okay if the batter is a bit lumpy. Overmixing develops gluten and results in tough muffins, so gentle folding preserves tenderness.
  5. Carefully fold in the fresh blueberries, being gentle to avoid crushing them. This keeps the berries intact so they don’t bleed too much into the batter, which keeps your muffins looking pretty and avoids a purple tint throughout.
  6. Divide the batter evenly among the muffin cups, filling each about 3/4 full. Using an ice cream scoop helps portion the batter for uniform muffins that bake evenly. Overfilling can cause overflow, and underfilling leads to flat muffins.
  7. Bake the muffins for about 20-25 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through for even baking. Test doneness by inserting a toothpick in the center; it should come out clean or with a few moist crumbs. Avoid opening the oven too early to prevent collapsing.
  8. Remove the muffins from the oven and let them cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely. This resting time allows the muffins to finish cooking and prevents sogginess from trapped steam.
  9. Serve warm or at room temperature. These muffins are delightful on their own or with a pat of butter or cream cheese. Store leftovers in an airtight container for freshness. Enjoying them slightly warm really brings out the flavors and moist texture.
